data.narrative:
DigiChem is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Greg Ellson and Ben Berman, having raised $4M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 9 private and 1 public comparable company, though narrow-stage peer data remains sparse for reliable multiples-based triangulation.

The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $4M raised proxy, implied by typical Seed-to-next-stage dynamics in frontier tech, yielding a $10M valuation. The peer-median approach was determined not applicable: while 11 robotics and manufacturing companies exist in the broader comp set (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI), filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier peers produced fewer than three datapoints—insufficient for reliable median calculation. A cross-sector median would introduce material skew and was therefore excluded.

The triangulation, drawing from one applied method, supports a valuation range of $8M to $12M, with a $10M median. Key uncertainties center on the scarcity of Seed-stage comparables within the robotics subsector and the absence of meaningful public market pricing signals (single public comp) for this stage and capital intensity profile. Sensitivity to market conditions and follow-on funding momentum remains high given the early stage and narrow methodological foundation.
